name: Holding Balancegrip
description: Hold the stave across the chest in both hands at shoulder width, steadying the stance and covering the torso.

name: Staffpace
description: Set the lead foot forward and the rear foot braced, so the body can rock between advance and retreat.

name: Straight Jabbing
description: Drive the near end of the stave straight at the opponent's chest, pushing from the rear leg.

name: Staffblow
description: Raise the stave over the shoulder and bring it down on the opponent's head or shoulder.

name: Angled Midstaff
description: Raise the stave horizontally in both hands to stop a downward blow against the shaft.

name: Steady Staffgrip
description: Slide the leading hand along the shaft while the rear hand pivots, shifting the stave's reach between long and short.

name: Shifting Staffshoe
description: Slide the front foot ahead and drag the rear foot after it, closing distance without crossing the feet.

name: Oakdodge
description: Push off the lead foot and draw the rear foot back, opening distance while the stave stays levelled.

name: Low Staffsweep
description: Swing the stave low and flat to rap the opponent's shin or knee.

name: Downward Quarterpoint
description: Whip the far end of the pole in a downward arc at the opponent's head.

name: Raised Ironcap
description: Lift the shaft upward and outward to knock aside a thrust or a swing.

name: Staffgauge
description: Raise and lower the stave overhead in slow repetitions, conditioning the shoulders and wrists for long sparring.

name: Firm Jabbing
description: Thrust the stave straight ahead in a rhythmic line of repeated stabs without lowering the guard.

name: Quick Staffspin
description: Strike the near arm twice in quick succession, pressing the opponent back a half step.

name: Square Oakstaff
description: Pivot on the lead foot and swing the rear end of the stave into the opponent's ribs.

name: Ready Midstaff
description: Hold the stave angled upward across the face and chest to cover the head from above.

name: Lowered Staffend
description: Drop the stave tip toward the ground at an angle to cover the legs from a low swing.

name: Ashskitter
description: Turn the hips off the line of attack and shift the feet, letting a blow pass by.

name: Planted Ironcap
description: Advance with the stave held diagonally across the body, covering the head and flank at every step.

name: Quiet Poleturn
description: Take a short fast step inside the opponent's reach while holding the stave level, so the guard travels with the body.

name: Oakdrop
description: Strike down at the head with a full arm swing, using the far third of the stave for the blow.

name: Wide Staffsweep
description: Swing the stave in a flat horizontal arc into the opponent's flank, turning from the hips.

name: Oakcowl
description: Parry a blow to the outside with the shaft and answer at once with a short strike.

name: Pushing Nodeknot
description: Press the stave against the opponent's weapon arm to shove it aside and spoil the next attack.

name: Backward Poleturn
description: Turn the body about the rear foot and swing the stave around, changing the facing to meet a flank attack.

name: Sharp Staffshoe
description: Hook the end of the stave behind an advancing heel and pull sharply to unbalance the opponent.

name: Solid Oakstaff
description: Plant the stave on the ground at an angle and lean into it, bracing against a shove or a charge.

name: Narrow Midstaff
description: Thrust the stave along a narrow lane, keeping the body in line so there is little room to be flanked.

name: Level Staffsweep
description: Swing the stave in a wide low arc at knee height, sweeping the opponent's lead leg.

name: Kept Nodeknot
description: Hold the stave upright at arm's length and knock a blow aside as a fence rail would.

name: Rowanhop
description: Drop at the knees under a swing while keeping the stave raised over the head.

name: Ashhit
description: Flex the shaft with both hands at the end of a downward swing so the tip lands faster on the target.

name: Leaden Staffend
description: Shift the grip toward the lighter end so the heavy end carries the blow into the opponent's torso.

name: Catching Staffgrip
description: Slide the stave along the opponent's weapon and catch it in the crook of the hand to stop its swing.

name: Blunt Rapidspin
description: Snap the wrists in a short flicking rap that stings the opponent's hands and forces a flinch.

name: Ashwedge
description: Plant the stave butt on the ground and hold it upright to ward off a charge.

name: Snug Quarterpoint
description: Settle the stave across the body and breathe a thread of qi into the grip, steadying the guard for longer.

name: Light Midstaff
description: Time a forward step to the breath, carrying a trickle of qi through the legs so the advance is smooth.

name: Open Jabbing
description: Thrust the near end of the stave at the opponent's chest, adding a pulse of qi at the moment of contact.

name: Flat Staffsweep
description: Sweep the stave in a flat arc at waist height, letting qi stiffen the shaft against a block.

name: Folded Ironcap
description: Lift the stave to meet a blow and flick it aside, tightening the grip with a brief burst of qi.

name: Stiff Rollover
description: Rebound the stave off a parry and strike back along the same line before the opponent recovers.

name: Perchstrike
description: Turn the hips and swing the stave diagonally downward, adding qi to the arms to deepen the strike.

name: Gentle Balancegrip
description: Roll the stave in small circles from the wrists, drawing qi along the forearms to loosen the grip.

name: Upward Rapidspin
description: Roll the stave in a flowing figure eight before the body, a screen of motion that makes the opponent hesitate.

name: Resting Ashwood
description: Spin the stave overhead in a flat wheel to deflect blows aimed at the head or shoulders.

name: Hooding Oakstaff
description: Spin the stave at the side of the body in a vertical wheel, covering the flank.

name: Sideways Poleturn
description: Step in a small circle while the stave wheels, so the body changes angle without breaking the guard.

name: Short Poleturn
description: Finish a turning wheel by driving the near end into the opponent's mid-line.

name: Turning Rapidspin
description: Wind the stave around the opponent's weapon in a quick circle and wrench it away.

name: Quick Staffend
description: Reverse the wheel and bring the trailing end of the stave across in a short return strike.

name: Staffstay
description: Hold the stave in the first guard, tip forward and level, and let a faint breath of qi settle into the hands.

name: Rowanbump
description: Thrust from the first guard with a steady push of the rear leg, a thread of qi reaching the tip.

name: Wide Rollover
description: Swing the stave in a wide arc from the shoulder, qi easing the follow-through.

name: Perchtrot
description: Step off the line of attack and turn, bringing the stave back to guard on the new line.

name: Settled Staffgrip
description: Let the leading hand slide along the shaft to meet a blow and push it aside.

name: Locking Staffshoe
description: Tap the opponent's weapon sharply and press the stave across it to hold it down.

name: Staffdash
description: Strike with the far end of the stave at full extension, trailing qi along the shaft into the blow.

name: Sudden Jabbing
description: Pull the hands to the middle and jab with the short end when the opponent steps inside the reach.

name: Warm Ashwood
description: Reverse the stave in the hands in one smooth motion, qi moving with the grip to change which end leads.

name: Skipping Staffend
description: Step back out of the opponent's reach and sweep the stave around to keep the distance.

name: Towing Staffshoe
description: Hook the far end behind the opponent's lead ankle and tug, qi tightening the grip to throw the balance off.

name: Tight Oakstaff
description: Parry a close attack with the short end of the stave, knocking the opponent's wrist aside.

name: Hard Staffspin
description: Strike with the long end, switch, and strike again with the short, a rapid pair that presses the opponent back.

name: Perchlid
description: Plant the stave butt and lean the shaft forward against a charge, qi hardening the arms for the brace.

name: Nimble Ironcap
description: Keep a low steady step under a heavy load, a thread of qi in the legs holding the stave levelled.

name: Oakstrike
description: Thrust the stave out from the walking stance without halting, qi gathering briefly at the tip.

name: Forward Staffsweep
description: Sweep the stave in a flat arc to clear an attacker from a narrow path.

name: Rowanhusk
description: Raise the stave level with the shoulder to block a blow at head height.

name: Raised Balancegrip
description: Draw breath as the stave rises to guard, letting qi gather in the arms ready for the next motion.

name: Rowandrop
description: Exhale sharply while thrusting the stave, so the qi releases at the moment of impact.

name: Downward Staffspin
description: Hold the breath through a heavy downward swing, packing qi into the arms before the blow lands.

name: Ashnote
description: Pulse a thread of qi along the shaft and into the tip, stiffening it for the following strike.

name: Swaying Rollover
description: Step back on the exhale and bring the stave to guard on the inhale, resetting distance and balance together.

name: Holding Midstaff
description: Match the parry to the rhythm of the breath, turning a blow aside on the exhale.

name: Solid Balancegrip
description: Hold the guard for a count of breaths while the qi circulates evenly through the arms.

name: Rowanlid
description: Tap the opponent's weapon hand at the end of an exhale, breaking its grip at the last moment.
